Remove the one animal of an affected status that shrinks a pedigree most

Source: R/findAvailAffected.R
findAvailAffected.Rd

One round of shrinkPedigree's third trim on the pedigree it is given. Among the genotyped animals that are no animal's parent and whose affected status is affstatus, it removes the one whose removal leaves the smallest bit size (see bitSize), with any animal that removal leaves removable as in the first trim (see findUnavailable): an ungenotyped parent left as a leaf, an ungenotyped founder couple left with one child, a founder left with no offspring. Ties go to the first id in byte order (capitals before lower case), whatever the computer's language setting, as in shrinkPedigree(); kinship2 breaks ties at random.

Usage

findAvailAffected(ped, genotyped, affected, affstatus)

Arguments

ped

a pedigree data.frame with the fields id, sire and dam, and optionally a logical affected column.

genotyped

a logical vector, one value per row of ped, TRUE where the animal is genotyped (or otherwise available). NA is not allowed.

affected

NULL or a logical vector, one value per row of ped. When NULL, ped$affected is used if it exists, and otherwise every animal counts as unaffected (FALSE). The numbers 1 and 0 read as TRUE and FALSE; any other number stops.

affstatus

the affected status of the animals to choose from: NA, FALSE or TRUE.

Value

A list, with kinship2::findAvailAffected()'s names:

ped

The pedigree after the removal, every column kept; id, sire and dam as character, and an animal made a founder has its sire and dam set to NA. When nothing is removed, ped with every row.

idTrimmed

Character vector, every id removed, in the order removed; character(0) when none is.

isTrimmed

TRUE when an animal was removed; FALSE when no genotyped non-parent has that status.

bitSize

Integer, the bit size of the returned ped.

Details

shrinkPedigree() tries an NA status first, then FALSE, then TRUE, and repeats until the bit size is within its maxBits. Called the same way on the pedigree its first two trims leave (shrinkPedigree(ped, genotyped, maxBits = Inf)$ped), this function makes the same removals.

It stops with shrinkPedigree()'s message for a bad pedigree, or for a genotyped or affected vector of the wrong length, or an NA in genotyped, and when affstatus is not one of NA, FALSE and TRUE.

References

Sinnwell JP, Therneau TM, Schaid DJ (2014). "The kinship2 R Package for Pedigree Data." Human Heredity, 78(2), 91-93.

See also

shrinkPedigree, findUnavailable, findAvailNonInform, bitSize

Examples

## K and M are genotyped non-parents of unknown affected status. Removing K
## also removes its ungenotyped sire P and leaves its dam Q a founder with
## no offspring, so the bit size falls from 5 to 2; removing M leaves 3.
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("GA", "GB", "P", "K", "Q", "L", "M"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "GA", "P", NA, "GA", "GA"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "GB", "Q", NA, "GB", "GB"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
genotyped <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
affected <- c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, NA, FALSE, TRUE, NA)
result <- findAvailAffected(ped, genotyped, affected, NA)
result$idTrimmed
#> [1] "K" "P" "Q"
result$bitSize
#> [1] 2
